Rashi on Shabbat 78a:1:1.hebrew: וליתא לדרבי ינאי - ור' שמעון בן אלעזר "או או" קתני: או אבר קטן של גדול, או להפך — וכולה חד שיעורא הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 78a:1:1.english: And [the opinion] of Rabbi Yannai is rejected - And Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar teaches "either... or": either a small limb of an adult, or the reverse [a large limb of a day-old child]; and it is all one measure.

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:1:2.hebrew: ת"ש כו' - ודרבי ינאי תנאי היא:
Rashi on Shabbat 78a:1:2.english: Come and hear, etc. - And [the opinion] of Rabbi Yannai is [a dispute between] Tannaim.

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:2:1.hebrew: מכדי כל מילתא דשכיחא ולא שכיחא - כל ששיערו חכמים לענין שבת, והוא ראוי לשני דברים — חדא שכיחא וחדא לא שכיחא — אזול רבנן בשיעורן בתר דשכיחא. ואפילו היא קולא, ששיעורה גדול, אמרינן: סתמיה להא עביד, ולא אמרי': הואיל וחזי נמי למילתא אחריתי ששיעורה קטן, ניזיל בתרה לחומרא, ואע"פ דלא שכיחא:
Rashi on Shabbat 78a:2:1.english: Now, since, [with regard to] any matter that is common and uncommon - Anything that the Sages established a measure for regarding Shabbat, and it is suitable for two purposes — one [of which] is common and one [of which] is uncommon — the Sages followed that which is common in [determining] their measure. And even [if] it is a leniency, where its measure is large, we say: Ordinarily, it is used for this; and we do not say: Since it is also suitable for another purpose whose measure is small, let us follow it as a stringency, even though it is uncommon.

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:2:2.hebrew: שכיחא ושכיחא - והיכא דשכיחי תרוייהו, אזלינן לחומרא ומשערינן בשיעורא זוטא:
Rashi on Shabbat 78a:2:2.english: [Where one is] common and [the other is] common - And where both of them are common, we follow the stringency and measure by the smaller measure.

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:3:1.hebrew: רפואתו לא שכיחא - כגון לשוף בו קילור. ואע"ג דחזי לה — דאיכא דעביד בחלב אשה ואיכא דעביד במיא, וחסין על היין שדמיו יקרים. הלכך, אזול בתר שתייתו ושיערוהו בכדי מזיגת כוס, ואע"ג דלקולא — שיש כאן שיעור גדול. וכן חלב נמי חזי לאכילה ולשוף קילור, ומיהו לא שכיחא, שהרי אף המים ראויין לכך ויש עושין ממים. הלכך, אזול רבנן בתר אכילתו, ושיעורו בכדי גמיאה, ואע"ג דקולא היא:
Rashi on Shabbat 78a:3:1.english: Its [use for] healing is uncommon - Such as to dissolve eye-salve with it. And even though it is fit for this [purpose, it is uncommon], as there are some who do [so] with woman’s milk and there are some who do [so] with water, and people are sparing with wine, since its cost is high. Therefore, they followed its [use for] drinking and measured it as enough to dilute a cup [of wine] — even though [this leads] to a leniency, as there is a large measure here. And likewise, milk is also fit for consumption and for dissolving eye-salve; but nevertheless, [its use for healing] is uncommon, for even water is fit for this, and there are those who make [it] with water. Therefore, the Sages followed its consumption, and its measure is enough for a swallow, even though it is a leniency.

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:3:2.english: Honey, its use for healing is also common - For no other liquid is suitable for a sore.

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:3:3.hebrew: לחומרא - הואיל ותרוייהו שכיחן, לחומרא בעינן לשעוריה:
Rashi on Shabbat 78a:3:3.english: As a stringency - Since both are common, we must determine its measure stringently.

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:4:1.hebrew: רפואתו לא שכיחא - שהרי שאר משקין ראויין לכך, ויש שפין קילור בשאר משקין. ושתייתו שכיחא — שרוב שתיית מים הם, שאין אדם שותה יין לכל צמאיו, כי אם לסעודתו:
Rashi on Shabbat 78a:4:1.english: Its medicinal use is uncommon - For other liquids are suitable for this, and there are those who dissolve collyrium [eye salve] in other liquids. And its drinking is common — for most drinking is of water, as a person does not drink wine for all his thirst, but only for his meal.

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:4:2.hebrew: בגלילא שנו - שהן עניים ומקפידין בדבר מועט, וחסין על יין וחלב לשוף קילור, ואין שפין אלא במים. והלכך, רפואתו נמי שכיחא, ובעינן למיזל לחומרא:
Rashi on Shabbat 78a:4:2.english: They taught [this] in the Galilee - For they are poor and particular about [even] a small thing, and spare wine and milk [rather than using them] to dissolve eye-salve, and they only dissolve [it] with water. Therefore, its [use for] healing is also common, and we must follow the stringency.

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:4:3.english: All liquids - All liquids with which one rubs eye salve.

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:4:5.hebrew: ומטללי - מסככין על העין ומונעין מראיתו, עד שיכלה מראיתו לגמרי, מפני שהן עבין ונגלדין כמין דבק שקורין גלוזייר:
Rashi on Shabbat 78a:4:5.english: And cloud - They form a screen over the eye and impede its vision, until its vision is completely gone, because they are thick and form a crust like a type of glue, which is called gluzier [glue].

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:4:6.hebrew: בר ממיא - דעדיפי מכולהו, דמסו ולא מטללי, שנבלעין מיד או ניגבין מהר, ולא נגלדין על גב העין:
Rashi on Shabbat 78a:4:6.english: Except for water - Which is superior to all of them, as it heals and does not cloud [the vision], for it is absorbed immediately or dries quickly, and does not form a crust over the eye.

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:5:1.english: For they paint [the eye] for barkit - Maille [an eye disease], which protrudes on the eye.

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:5:2.english: And what are they - From which blood do they apply [kohl] to it?

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:5:3.hebrew: ליארוד - תבלול. ובתוספתא ראיתי לחורור, והן טיפות דקות של לובן הנולדות בעין, כדתנן בבכורות גבי מומין (דף לח:):
Rashi on Shabbat 78a:5:3.english: For a cataract - [Meaning,] a tevallul [a white ocular defect]. And in the Tosefta I saw [the reading] “for chivror”; and these are fine droplets of white that develop in the eye, as we learned in the Mishnah in Bekhorot regarding blemishes (daf 38b).

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:5:4.english: The blood of a kerushtina - A bat [or: mole], which is called talpe [Old French for mole].

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:5:5.hebrew: גוא - כרושתינא מצוי בתוך היישוב, שהוא ליארוד, שהוא שוקע בתוך העין:
Rashi on Shabbat 78a:5:5.english: Inside - The bat is found inside the settlement, which is [used] for yarod [a cataract], which is sunken inside the eye.

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:5:6.hebrew: לברא - דמא דתרנגולת ברא לברקית, שהיא בולטת:
Rashi on Shabbat 78a:5:6.english: For the outside - The blood of a wild chicken [is] for barkit, which protrudes.

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:6:1.hebrew: בד"א - דבעינן שיעורא במוציא לר"ה:
Rashi on Shabbat 78a:6:1.english: In what case are these matters stated - That we require a [prescribed] measure [is] with regard to one who carries out into the public domain.

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:6:2.hebrew: אבל המצניע - והוציאו — חייב בכל שהוא. לקמיה פריך: אטו מצניע לאו מוציא הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 78a:6:2.english: However, one who stores - And [then] carried it out — he is liable for any amount. Later on, [the Gemara] asks: Is one who stores not [also] one who carries out?

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:6:3.hebrew: ר' שמעון אומר בד"א - דמיחייב בשיעורא זוטא כי האי:
Rashi on Shabbat 78a:6:3.english: Rabbi Shimon says: In what case are these matters stated - That one is liable for a small measure such as this.

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:6:4.english: With regard to one who stores - [One who stored] this measure and subsequently carried it out.

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:6:5.hebrew: אבל במוציא - אדם שלא הצניעו והוציאו, אינו חייב אלא ברביעית:
Rashi on Shabbat 78a:6:5.english: However, with regard to one who carries [it] out - A person who did not store it and carried it out is liable only for a quarter [of a log].

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:6:6.hebrew: במוציא שופכין - אדם שלא הצניען אינו חייב אלא ברביעית, דבציר מהכי לא חזו — כדלקמן — לגבל טיט:
Rashi on Shabbat 78a:6:6.english: [With regard to] one who carries out waste water - A person who did not store it is liable only for a quarter [of a log], for less than this is not fit — as [explained] below — to knead mortar.

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:7:1.english: Is one who stores not one who carries out? - For is one not liable only by means of carrying out?

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:7:2.hebrew: אמר אביי הכא בתלמיד - כגון שולי דנגרי, שאומר לו רבו: לך ופנה לי המקום:
Rashi on Shabbat 78a:7:2.english: Abaye said: Here [we are dealing] with a student - For example, a carpenter’s apprentice, whose master says to him: “Go and clear the place for me.”

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:7:3.english: An item that is significant to all, he is liable for it - Even though his teacher did not store it for his [own] need.

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:7:4.hebrew: דבר שאינו חשוב לכל כו' - והכי קאמרי: בד"א דבעינן שעורא דחשיב — במוציא; כלומר, בדבר שאין לך לילך בו אלא אחר הוצאתו של זה, שהמחשבה תלויה בזה שהוציא. אבל במצניע — בדבר שיש לך לילך אחר מחשבה של מצניע; כגון המצניע כל שהוא, חייב זה המוציאו. ורשב"א אמרה, ואזיל לטעמיה, דאמר בפרקין דלעיל: דבדבר שאין מצניעין כמוהו, והוכשר לזה והצניעו — נתחייב זה במחשבתו של זה. וה"ה דמצי לאוקמי במצניע גופיה, ולמימר הכי: בד"א במוציא — בדבר שלא הוצנע, ואין לך לילך בו אלא אחר הוצאתו של זה; אבל אם היה זה מצניע דבר זה מתחילה וחזר והוציאו — חייב. אלא משום דשמעי' לי' דאמר "נתחייב זה במחשבה של זה", אוקמא אביי אפי' באחר שהוציאו, וכ"ש אם הוציאו הוא עצמו:
Rashi on Shabbat 78a:7:4.english: An item that is not significant to all, etc. - And this is what [the Baraita] means to say: “In what case are these matters stated” — that we require a measure that is significant [to all]? “With regard to one who carries out” — that is to say, regarding an item where you have nothing to go by other than this person’s act of carrying out, for the [determining] intent depends on this person who carried [it] out; “however, with regard to one who stores” — regarding an item where you have to go by the intent of the storer, such as [where the master] stored any amount, this person who carries it out is liable. And Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar stated it [this Baraita], and he follows his own reasoning, as he said in our chapter above: that regarding an item like which people do not store, but it was deemed fit for this person and he stored it, this one [who carries it out] is rendered liable by that one’s intent. And by the same token, [Abaye] could have established [the Baraita] with regard to the storer himself, and said like this: “In what case are these matters stated?” With regard to one who carries out an item that had not been stored, where you have nothing to go by other than this person’s act of carrying out; but if this person had stored this item initially and then went back and carried it out, he is liable. However, because we have heard him saying: “This one is rendered liable by that one’s intent,” Abaye established it even where another person carried it out, and all the more so if he carried it out himself.

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:8:1.hebrew: פי כור - נקב שנותנין בו המפוח, ושיעורא זוטא הוא, ומרביעית חזי לגבל טובא. וכיון דהוצאת טיט חשיבא בכדי פי כור, בעינן נמי לשעוריה בהנך דעבדי לטיט בכדי גיבול פי כור:
Rashi on Shabbat 78a:8:1.english: The opening of a crucible - The hole into which one places the bellows; and it is a small measure, and from a quarter [of a log] it is sufficient to knead a great deal [of clay]. And since carrying out clay is considered significant with [an amount] sufficient for the opening of a crucible, we should also require measuring it, for those who make clay, by [the amount needed for] kneading [clay for] the opening of a crucible.

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:8:2.hebrew: דמיגבל - כבר חשוב בכדי פי כור, אבל זה שעדיין לא נגבל — אינו נשער בכך, לפי שאין אדם טורח לגבל שיעור מועט כזה; ואם בא לגבל — מגבל יותר, ועושה בו דברים אחרים:
Rashi on Shabbat 78a:8:2.english: That is kneaded - [Having] already [been kneaded], it is significant [in an amount] enough for the opening of a crucible; but that which is not yet kneaded is not measured by this [amount], because a person does not take the trouble to knead such a small quantity, and if he comes to knead, he kneads more and makes other things with it.

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:9:1.english: An ear for a basket - To hold [the basket] by it.

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:9:2.english: A loop for hanging - To hang [the utensil] by it.

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:9:3.hebrew: מדת מנעל - להראותו לאומן: "כמדה זו אני צריך":
Rashi on Shabbat 78a:9:3.english: The measure of a shoe - To show [it] to the craftsman: “I need [a shoe] of this measure.”

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:9:4.english: Paper - They make it from plants.

Rashi on Shabbat 78a:9:5.hebrew: קשר של מוכסין - יש לך אדם שנותן המכס לראש הנהר במקום אחד, או מוחל לו במתנה, והוא מוסר לו חותם להראות למוכס שמחל לו המכס. ודרכו לכתוב בו שתי אותיות, והן גדולות משתי אותיות שלנו:
Rashi on Shabbat 78a:9:5.english: A tax collectors’ receipt - There is a person who pays the customs duty at the head of the river in one place, or [the collector] waives it for him as a gift, and he hands him a seal to show the tax collector that he waived the customs duty for him. And it is customary to write two letters on it, and they are larger than two of our letters.

Tosafot on Shabbat 78a:5:1.hebrew: דם וכל מיני משקין ברביעית - בתוספתא גרס: "ושאר מיני משקין". וכן נראה, דהא כל מיני משקין אינן ברביעית, דיין ושמן ודבש ומים — שיעורן כדתנן במתני':
Tosafot on Shabbat 78a:5:1.english: "Blood and all types of liquids are a quarter-log" - In the Tosefta, the text reads: "And other types of liquids." And so it appears [correct], for not all types of liquids are [measured at] a quarter-log, as [with] wine, oil, honey, and water — their measures are as we learned in the Mishnah.

Tosafot on Shabbat 78a:5:2.hebrew: שכן כוחלין ליארוד - אין נראה לר"י לפרש דהיינו תבלול, דבתוספת' קתני בהך מילתא גופא שכוחלים לחורור, ובבכורות (דף לח:) חשיב תבלול וחורור; אלמא תבלול לאו היינו חורור:
Tosafot on Shabbat 78a:5:2.english: "As one applies [blood] for yarod" - It does not appear to the Ri to explain that this is tevallul, for in the Tosefta it teaches regarding this very matter that one applies [blood] for choror, and in Bekhorot (38b) [the Mishnah] lists [both] tevallul and choror; evidently, tevallul is not [the same as] choror.

Tosafot on Shabbat 78a:7:1.hebrew: אטו מצניע לאו מוציא הוא - פירש בקונט': דהוה מצי למימר, "הב"ע כשהצניעו והוציאו", אלא דניחא ליה לישנויי בשלא הוציאו המצניע עצמו, משום דאתיא כרשב"א. וקשה: דמנלן דאתיא כרשב"א? אדרבה, כרשב"ג אתיא, דמיירי לבסוף! ועוד, דאמאי נקט "בתלמיד שא"ל רבו"? אפילו אדם בעלמא נמי! ודוחק לומר, דלא מחייב רבי שמעון במחשבתו של זה אלא תלמיד במחשבתו של רבו. לכך נראה, דה"פ: "אטו מצניע לאו מוציא הוא?" — דמדלא קתני "אבל המצניע בכל שהוא", דהוה משמע דהמצניע הוא המוציא, כדדייק לעיל: "אינו חייב אלא המצניעו", מתניתין דלא כרשב"א, אלא קתני "במצניע", משמע: אפילו אחר הצניעו חייב המוציא. ולהכי קשיא ליה: "אטו מצניע לאו מוציא הוא?" דהא שום תנא לא מחייב, אא"כ הוציאו המצניע, אלא רשב"א לבדו, ומתניתין דכלל גדול (לעיל שבת עה:) דהמצניע — דלא כוותיה! ומשני: "בתלמיד שאמר לו רבו", דכה"ג כ"ע מודו, שהתלמיד עושה הכל לדעת רבו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 78a:7:1.english: Is the one who stores not the one who carries out? - Rashi explained that [the Gemara] could have said: "Here we are dealing with [a case where] he stored it and [then] carried it out [himself]." But it was preferable to [the Gemara] to resolve it [as referring to a case] where the one who stored it did not carry it out himself, because [this baraita] follows Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar. And this is difficult: From where do we know that it follows Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar? On the contrary, it follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, who spoke last! And furthermore, why did [Abaye] formulate [the case as referring] to a student whose teacher said to him [to clear space]? Even an ordinary person [who carried it out should] also [be liable, according to Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar]! And it is forced to say that Rabbi Shimon [ben Elazar] holds [a person] liable based on another's intention only [in the case of] a student [acting] with the intention of his teacher. Therefore, it appears that this is the explanation: "Is the one who stores not the one who carries out?" — for since it did not teach: "However, the one who stores [hamatznia] is liable for any amount" — which would imply that the one who stores is the one who carries it out, as [the Gemara] deduced above (76a): "Only the one who stores it is liable," [proving that] our Mishnah is not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar — but rather taught: "with regard to storing [bematznia]," which implies that even if another person stored it, the one who carries it out is liable. And for this reason it was difficult to [the Gemara]: "Is the one who stores not [the one who must be] the one who carries out?!" For indeed, no tanna holds [a person] liable unless the one who stored it carried it out, except for Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar alone, and the Mishnah of Klal Gadol (above, Shabbat 75b) [concerning] the one who stores is not in accordance with him! And [Abaye] answers: [We are dealing] with a student whose teacher said to him [to clear space], for in such a case everyone agrees, as the student does everything according to the intention of his teacher.

Tosafot on Shabbat 78a:8:1.hebrew: שופכין למאי חזו - דוקא אברייתא קא בעי; וכן משמע לקמן (שבת דף עט.), דאמר: "והא טיט דמקמי דליגבליה תנא: מודים חכמים לרבי שמעון במוציא שופכין כו', והוינן בה: שופכין למאי חזו?" — משמע דבמתני' אתי שפיר. ונרא' לר"י דהיינו טעמא: משום דשופכין דמתניתין איכא למימר דחזו לכמה דברים, לרחוץ בהם כוסות וקערות, דלא מאיסי כולי האי, אלא שאינן ראויין לשתיה; אבל הכא דומיא דדם קתני, דמאיסי טובא, ולכך בעי: למאי חזו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 78a:8:1.english: For what is waste water fit - [The Gemara] asks [this] specifically on the baraita; and so it is implied below (Shabbat 79a), where it says: "And isn't there clay, which before one kneads it, [the tanna] taught: The Rabbis agree with Rabbi Shimon with regard to one who carries out waste water, etc., and we discussed it: For what is waste water fit?" — which implies that regarding the Mishnah, it works out well. And it appears to the Ri that this is the reason: Because regarding the waste water of the Mishnah, it can be said that it is fit for several things, [such as] to rinse cups and bowls with it, for it is not so repulsive, but rather is merely unfit for drinking; but here, it is taught similar to blood, [meaning] that it is very repulsive, and therefore [the Gemara] asks: For what is it fit?
